title: Prefetch Escrow and SLA Commitment Playbook
author: Asha Kumar
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a standard for providing short-term, bounded prefetch (\"warmset\") escrow commitments to tenants, documenting operational mechanics, SLO/SLA contracts, dashboarding requirements, alerts, and experiment/rollback criteria. The goal is to balance product-level latency guarantees for high-value customers while preserving multi-tenant fairness and cost transparency.

Audience: Platform operators, platform engineering, product managers owning tenant SLAs, and oncall responders.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to all multitenant GPU-backed inference pools (hosted and dedicated) that expose prefetching/long-lived warmsets.
- Covers: escrow allocation, monitoring, billing signal integration, operator workflows, and canary/experiment phases for new escrow policies.
- Excludes: one-off on-prem packages where customer agreements explicitly define a different mechanism.

Key definitions

- Warmset: in-memory KV / prefix cache reserved to accelerate model generation for an active session.
- Escrow: temporary reservation of warmset capacity (memory + hot GPU context slots) on behalf of a tenant for N minutes/hours.
- Escrow Commitment (short): company commitment to maintain X MB of warmset for Y minutes at a given priority tier.
- Escrow Budget: accounting primitive tracked per tenant for short-term reservations.

SLA / SLO matrix (operator-facing view)

| Commitment Tier | Typical warmset size | Guaranteed time window | Latency uplift target | Burn priority | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Bronze | 32MB | 5 minutes | <= +15% vs baseline | low | best-effort, used for free-tier trials |
| Silver | 128MB | 15 minutes | <= +8% vs baseline | medium | billed per-minute above baseline |
| Gold | 512MB | 60 minutes | <= +3% vs baseline | high | contractual, alerting to SRE on >5% breach |

Operational guarantees are expressed per-region and per-GPU-class (A100/H100). Baseline measured as the 95th percentile latency for equivalent tenant tier without prefetch.

Escrow mechanics (runtime and accounting)

1. Reservation API (control plane): tenants request escrow via /v1/escrow POST { tenant_id, size_mb, duration_minutes, priority_tier }. The control plane validates quota and either issues a reservation token or returns a candidate window with alternative capacity.
2. Runtime allocation: reservation tokens map to a warmset shard. The runtime pins a shard and marks metadata: {reservation_id, expires_at, owner_tenant, size_mb, region, model_variant}.
3. Eviction rules: expirations, priority-based preemption (low -> medium -> high), and operator-initiated drain. Preemption must respect safety delays (default 30s) and notify tenants through the control plane callback webhooks.
4. Billing / cost attribution: every reservation emits a metering event: escrow.reserve/escrow.release/escrow.preempt. These events join token-cost attribution pipelines and billing reconciliation.

Dashboard and alerting requirements

Minimum dashboards (per-region):
- Escrow utilization heatmap (time vs size): shows active reservations, queued requests, preemption events.
- Escrow latency impact SLO panel: baseline vs observed p50/p95 token latencies for impacted tenants.
- Escrow cost signal: cumulative minutes-reserved * per-minute price by tenant and by pool.
- Escrow preemption funnel: requests -> granted -> expired -> preempted.

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- Escrow-Utilization-High (warning): total reserved capacity > 75% of pool for > 5m. Notify: platform-operators Slack + paging for Gold-secondaries.
- Escrow-Preemption-Rate (critical): > 5 preemptions/min sustained for 10m in a pool. Pager to SRE.
- Escrow-SLO-Drift (warning): any Gold-tier tenant p95 latency > SLA target for 3 consecutive 5m windows. Pager to responsible team and ops-runbook owner.

Alert data payloads must include: reservation_id(s), tenant_id(s), pool_id, region, recent-5m p50/p95 latencies, cost impact estimate.

Operator runbook: triage and immediate actions

1. Receive alert -> cluster / kube filter for pool_id. Retrieve active reservations (control-plane API: GET /v1/escrow?pool_id=).
2. If Escrow-Preemption-Rate critical: check recent eviction logs: /var/log/runtime/evictions or runtime tracing. Identify preemption initiator (autoscaler vs operator vs emergency reclaim).
3. If Escrow-SLO-Drift: determine if drift is caused by (a) model variant change, (b) pool saturation, (c) network/regional degradation, or (d) cache corruption. Use this checklist:
   a. Confirm model checksum matches pinned model for reservation.
   b. Inspect GPU and memory metrics (util%, thermal_throttle, NVLINK errors).
   c. Check KV prefix cache error counters and serving runtime stack traces.
4. Remediation (ordered):
   - For (b) pool saturation: trigger ephemeral-burst expansion (if enabled) OR initiate targeted preemptions of Bronze reservations using the preemption API to lower total reserved size.
   - For (d) cache corruption: trigger a soft-drain on affected warmset shards, clear prefix cache for reservation_id, and rehydrate via a synthetic warmup request (curl example below).
   - For (a/c) variant or network: roll fallback to previous model variant via rollout API and invalidate affected reservations for reconciliation.

CLI snippet: synthetic warmup and reconciliation\\n
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/warmup \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"reservation_id":"rsv_1234","warmup_prompts":["Hey, summarize: ..."],"target_shard":"shard-7"}'

Operator safety rules

- Never preempt a Gold reservation unless automated safeguards show pool saturation and Gold preemption is configured as allowed. Document reasons and create a post-action ticket.
- Respect tenant callback deadlines: always send preemption notifications at least 30s before eviction unless emergency reclaim.
- When draining a shard, allow a cooldown window of 120s before reassigning the same shard to a different tenant to avoid hot-cache thrash.

Rollout checklist for two-week canary window (for a new escrow policy)

1. Stabilize experiment infra: deploy control plane feature flag off by default.
2. Week 0 (smoke): enable policy for internal tenants + gold-green customers (low traffic daytime window). Monitor heatmap and preemption funnel.
3. Week 1 (wider canary): add 10% production traffic from selected tenants. Enable detailed tracing and double-write metering to the experimental cost pipeline.
4. Week 2 (validation): run SLIs for Gold-tier: p95 latency delta, preemption count, billing divergence. Run automated abort if:
   - Gold p95 > SLA target for more than 3 consecutive 5m windows, OR
   - Escrow-Preemption-Rate > 3/min sustained for 15m, OR
   - Observed cost leakage > 20% over predicted.
5. Post-canary retrospective: complete template below within 48h.

Experiment matrix (recommended metrics)

- Metric: p95 token latency (Gold/Silver/Bronze) — Gate: no >3% regressions for Gold at p95
- Metric: Escrow grant ratio (requests/granted) — Gate: > 95% for Gold, > 80% for Silver
- Metric: Preemption latency (time between preempt decision and eviction) — Gate: median <= 35s
- Metric: Cost delta (predicted vs observed) — Gate: < 15% error at pool-level

Post-action retrospective template (to be filled by oncall and PM)

- Summary of changes tested (feature flags / config values)
- Key metrics (with charts attached): p50/p95 by tier, utilization, preemption funnel, billing delta
- Incidents observed (time, owner, remediation applied)
- Root cause analysis (if applicable)
- Action items (owner, due date): e.g. adjust preemption threshold, add dashboard panel, improve billing joins

Example audit table (human-readable)

| timestamp | reservation_id | tenant | size_mb | outcome | notes |
| 2026-01-18T03:12Z | rsv_2312 | acme-payments | 512 | preempted | preempted for pool reclaim due to thermal spike |
| 2026-01-19T14:04Z | rsv_2450 | internal-smoke | 32 | expired | normal |

Telemetry and instrumentation contract

Every reservation lifecycle must emit these events with consistent schema (JSON lines in the telemetry topic):
- escrow.requested {reservation_id, tenant_id, size_mb, requested_at, priority_tier}
- escrow.granted {reservation_id, shard_id, pool_id, granted_at, expires_at}
- escrow.preempted {reservation_id, reason, initiated_by, preempted_at}
- escrow.released {reservation_id, released_at, duration_seconds}

Instrumentation owners must ensure the following labels are present on telemetry: tenant_id, pool_id, gpu_class, region, feature_flag_version. Missing labels are automatic failure for canary promotion.

Billing reconciliation notes

- Metering events feed billing buckets in two places: near-real-time charge previews (for early-warning) and final billing ledger. Conservatively tag canary double-writes with "experimental":true to avoid accidental customer charges.
- Reconciliation job must join escrow events with token consumption and compute an effective per-minute escrow price that includes GPU occupancy cost + marginal warmset memory cost.

Escalation and communication playbook

- Pager -> SRE on critical preemption spikes. SRE will: post incident bridge, notify PMs for affected Gold tenants, and open a cross-functional incident ticket.
- For customer-impacting SLA breaches (Gold): Engineering lead + Account EM maintained Slack channel must be notified within 15 minutes with summary and mitigation plan.

Retrospective cadence and ownership

- After any Gold SLA incident, schedule a 2-hour RCA within 72 hours. Owner: platform-ops.
- Quarterly review of escrow economics and policy: product + finance + platform-ops. Owner: Platform Product Manager.

Roadmap items (next 12 months)

- Q2 2026: dynamic escrow autoscaling prototype — grow/shrink reserved warmset by short-term predictive load signals.
- Q3 2026: pricing tier revision and per-tenant throttling controls exposed in Console.
- Q4 2026: integrate escrow telemetry into cost-forecasting model and cross-tenant fairness detector.

Appendix: sample dashboards (Grafana panels)

- Panel: Escrow Utilization by Pool — query: sum(active_reserved_mb) by (pool_id) over time.
- Panel: Escrow Grant Latency Histogram — query: histogram(grant_latency_ms).
- Panel: Escrow Preemption Timeline — annotated with eviction events and operator actions.
